newsitem.title: USA: Riordan wins second term as Los Angeles mayor.
newsitem.headline: Riordan wins second term as Los Angeles mayor.

text.p: Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan easily won re-election as leader of the second-largest U.S. city as final votes were counted early Wednesday.

"Los Angeles deserves to be proud ... Los Angeles is back," Riordan declared in his victory speech Tuesday night, referring to setbacks the city has overcome including the 1992 riots, the recession and the 1994 earthquake.
Riordan took 61 percent of the votes; his opponent, former activist Tom Hayden, garnered 35 percent.

Hayden, who represents Los Angeles in the California state Senate, told supporters he still believed in his dream of making Los Angeles a more desirable city to live in. "We have to continue that dream because without that dream we are not human beings," he said.
Despite a spirited election campaign, voter turnout was one of the lowest ever for a mayoral election in the city, with less than 30 percent going to the polls.

Although Riordan, a wealthy businessman first elected in 1993 who accepts a salary of only $1 a year as mayor, is a Republican and Hayden a Democrat, the race was non-partisan. Riordan had the backing of several prominent local Democrats while there were a number of Republicans in Hayden's camp.

Hayden, who was once married to actress Jane Fonda when both were anti-Vietnam War activists, injected the only real note of acrimony into the campaign when he accused Riordan of being a "racist" -- a remark he quickly withdrew.
Hayden is a former head of the militant Students for a Democratic Society (SDS) and was part of the famous Chicago Seven trial of war protesters.
In another contest, James Hahn was voted in for a fourth term as Los Angeles city attorney, beating San Fernando Valley attorney Ted Stein by a margin of 62 percent to 38 percent.

Voters also pushed through an initiative to rewrite the city's 72-year-old charter, by 61 percent to 39 percent, and another measure that would raise $2.4 billion to repair and renovate ageing city schools, by 71 percent to 29 percent.
